subject: Economics
text: Damilola has limited income but several urgent wants. The economic problem illustrated is
explanation: Scarcity exists because human wants are numerous while the resources and income available to satisfy them are limited. Inflation, monopoly and depreciation describe different economic situations.

subject: Economics
text: The value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made is called
explanation: Opportunity cost is the benefit sacrificed from the most valuable alternative not chosen. It arises because resources can be used in competing ways.

subject: Economics
text: A production possibility curve mainly shows the
options: Maximum alternative output combinations from given resources
explanation: A production possibility curve shows combinations of two goods that can be produced efficiently with available resources and technology. Points beyond it are unattainable with current capacity.

subject: Economics
text: According to the law of demand, other things being equal, quantity demanded rises when price
explanation: The law of demand states that consumers buy more at a lower price and less at a higher price, assuming other determinants such as income and taste remain unchanged.

subject: Economics
text: A change in quantity demanded caused solely by a change in the good’s own price is a
explanation: A price change causes movement from one point to another on the same demand curve. A shift occurs when a non-price determinant such as income or taste changes.

subject: Economics
text: Price falls from ₦51 to ₦49, while quantity demanded rises from 162 to 182 units. The approximate price elasticity of demand is
explanation: Price elasticity of demand equals percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price. The calculation measures responsiveness of quantity demanded to the price change.

subject: Economics
text: The law of supply states that producers are generally willing to offer more for sale when price
explanation: Higher prices usually make production more rewarding, so producers supply a larger quantity, other things being equal. This positive relationship is the law of supply.

subject: Economics
text: Market equilibrium occurs at the price where
explanation: At equilibrium, buyers wish to purchase exactly the quantity sellers wish to offer. There is neither a persistent shortage nor a surplus at that price.

subject: Economics
text: A maximum price fixed below the equilibrium price is most likely to create
explanation: A price ceiling below equilibrium makes the product cheaper, raising quantity demanded while reducing quantity supplied. The result is a shortage, also called excess demand.

subject: Economics
text: The factor of production that receives wages is
explanation: Labour refers to human effort used in production, and its reward is wages or salaries. Land earns rent, capital earns interest, and enterprise earns profit.

subject: Economics
text: A payment for a factory building that does not vary with output in the short run is a
explanation: Fixed costs remain unchanged as output changes in the short run, such as rent on a factory building. Variable costs change with the level of production.

subject: Economics
text: A firm has fixed cost of ₦92 and variable cost of ₦163 when it produces 10 units. Its average cost is
explanation: Average cost is total cost divided by output. Total cost is fixed cost plus variable cost, so ₦92 plus ₦163 divided by 10 units gives the stated average cost.

subject: Economics
text: An internal economy of scale arises when a firm reduces average cost because it
options: Expands its own scale of operation
explanation: Internal economies arise within an expanding firm, for example through specialization, bulk buying or technical efficiency. They reduce average cost as the firm grows.

subject: Economics
text: A market with many buyers and sellers, homogeneous products and free entry is closest to
explanation: Perfect competition is characterised by many small firms, identical products, free entry and exit, and no single firm controlling price. A monopoly has one dominant seller.

subject: Economics
text: A firm that is the sole supplier of a service with high barriers to entry is a
explanation: A monopoly exists where one firm is the sole seller and can restrict entry through legal, technical or economic barriers. It differs from a market with many competing firms.

subject: Economics
text: Gross Domestic Product measures the money value of final goods and services produced
options: Within a country during a period
explanation: GDP measures final output produced within a country’s geographical boundaries over a stated period. It includes output by resident and foreign-owned firms operating locally.

subject: Economics
text: Gross National Product differs from GDP because GNP includes
explanation: GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad. It accounts for income residents earn abroad minus income paid to foreign owners domestically.

subject: Economics
text: A sustained rise in the general price level is called
explanation: Inflation is a persistent increase in average prices across the economy, reducing the purchasing power of money. Deflation is the opposite movement in the general price level.

subject: Economics
text: A person able and willing to work but actively seeking a job without finding one is
explanation: Unemployment refers to people in the labour force who are willing and able to work, are seeking work, but cannot obtain a job. Students not seeking work are normally inactive.

subject: Economics
text: The function of money that makes prices easy to compare is
explanation: Money serves as a unit of account by providing a common measure for expressing and comparing prices. It also acts as medium of exchange and store of value.

subject: Economics
text: The institution that issues legal tender and acts as banker to government is the
explanation: A central bank issues currency, manages monetary policy and serves government and commercial banks. Commercial banks mainly accept deposits and make loans to customers.

subject: Economics
text: A commercial bank primarily creates credit by
explanation: Commercial banks create credit when they lend part of deposited funds while maintaining required reserves. They cannot independently print legal tender currency.

subject: Economics
text: Money held in a current account that can be withdrawn by cheque is called
explanation: A demand deposit is payable on demand and is usually operated through cheques, transfers or cards. A time deposit is held for an agreed period before withdrawal.

subject: Economics
text: A fall in the external value of a country’s currency is known as
explanation: Depreciation means the currency buys less foreign currency than before. It can make exports cheaper to foreigners and imports more expensive to domestic buyers.

subject: Economics
text: A country exports goods worth ₦275 billion and imports goods worth ₦183 billion. Its balance of trade is
explanation: Balance of trade equals exports minus imports. Since exports exceed imports by ₦92 billion, the country records a trade surplus of that amount.

subject: Economics
text: A tax imposed on imported goods to protect local producers is a
explanation: A tariff is a customs duty on imports. It raises the import price and may protect domestic producers, while a quota restricts quantity rather than imposing a tax.

subject: Economics
text: An import quota is a policy that
options: Limits the quantity of a good that may be imported
explanation: An import quota sets a maximum physical quantity of a good allowed into the country. It differs from a tariff, which is a tax on imports.

subject: Economics
text: Government revenue obtained from compulsory payments without direct benefit is
explanation: Taxation consists of compulsory levies imposed by government to finance public expenditure. A taxpayer does not receive a direct benefit equal to the tax paid.

subject: Economics
text: A tax system in which the proportion of income paid rises as income rises is
explanation: A progressive tax takes a higher percentage of income from higher-income earners. A regressive tax takes a larger proportion from lower incomes, while proportional rates stay constant.

subject: Economics
text: A government budget is in deficit when
explanation: A budget deficit occurs when planned or actual public spending is greater than government revenue. Revenue greater than expenditure produces a budget surplus.

subject: Economics
text: If the marginal propensity to save is 0.40, the simple investment multiplier is
explanation: In the simple Keynesian model, the multiplier equals 1 divided by the marginal propensity to save. Dividing 1 by 0.40 gives 2.

subject: Economics
text: Disposable income is income remaining to households after
explanation: Disposable income is the income households can spend or save after direct taxes and compulsory deductions have been paid. It supports consumption and saving decisions.

subject: Economics
text: A rise in real output per person together with improvement in welfare is best described as
explanation: Economic development includes sustained growth in real income and broader improvements in living standards, health, education and social welfare. Output growth alone may not capture these changes.

subject: Economics
text: Investment in education and training improves the quality of
explanation: Human capital is the stock of skills, knowledge and health embodied in people. Education and training increase workers’ productivity and earning potential.

subject: Economics
text: The reward for an entrepreneur who organizes other factors and bears risk is
explanation: The entrepreneur coordinates land, labour and capital, takes business risk and receives profit as the reward. Rent, wages and interest reward land, labour and capital respectively.

subject: Economics
text: A rightward shift of the demand curve for a normal good may result from
options: A fall in the product price only
A rise in production cost only
explanation: For a normal good, higher consumer income increases demand at every possible price, shifting the demand curve right. A change in the good’s own price causes movement along the curve.

subject: Economics
text: An increase in the cost of raw materials is most likely to
options: Increase quantity supplied at every price
explanation: Higher input costs make production less profitable at each price, so producers offer less. This is shown by a leftward shift of the supply curve.

subject: Economics
text: The balance of payments records
options: A country’s economic transactions with the rest of the world
explanation: The balance of payments is a systematic record of transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world, including goods, services, income and capital flows.

subject: Economics
text: Terms of trade improve when
options: Import prices rise faster than export prices
Export prices rise relative to import prices
explanation: Terms of trade compare export prices with import prices. When export prices rise relative to import prices, a country can obtain more imports for a given quantity of exports.

subject: Economics
text: Government action that changes taxation or public expenditure to influence aggregate demand is
explanation: Fiscal policy uses government spending and taxation to influence economic activity. Monetary policy uses money supply, interest rates and related central-bank instruments.

subject: Economics
text: A central bank can reduce excessive credit expansion by
options: Printing more currency for all banks
explanation: A higher bank rate makes borrowing by commercial banks more expensive and tends to raise lending rates, discouraging credit expansion. Lower reserves usually have the opposite effect.

subject: Economics
text: The minimum fraction of deposits commercial banks must keep instead of lending is the
explanation: The reserve requirement is the legally or prudentially required portion of deposits that banks must retain as reserves. It helps protect liquidity and influences credit creation.

subject: Economics
text: A consumer cooperative is formed mainly to
options: Buy goods for members at favourable terms
explanation: A consumer cooperative pools members’ buying power to obtain goods at fair prices and may return surplus to members. It is not a monetary or tax authority.

subject: Economics
text: Pollution from a factory that affects nearby residents without compensation is a
explanation: A negative externality is an external cost imposed on third parties who are not directly involved in the transaction. Pollution can harm health and property without being included in market price.

subject: Economics
text: Street lighting is often provided by government because it is largely
explanation: Street lighting has public-good characteristics: one person’s use does not significantly reduce availability to others, and it is difficult to exclude non-payers.

subject: Economics
text: A country gains from specialization when it concentrates on goods it can produce at
options: The lowest wage in every sector
explanation: Comparative advantage is based on lower opportunity cost. By specializing in such goods and trading, countries can increase total output and consumption possibilities.

subject: Economics
text: The main statutory role of a central bank in an economy includes
explanation: The central bank manages monetary policy, currency and banking-system stability. Production decisions and elections lie outside its statutory monetary responsibilities.

subject: Economics
text: If a consumer price index rises from 131 to 143, the inflation rate is approximately
explanation: Inflation rate is the percentage rise in the price index: (143 − 131) divided by 131, multiplied by 100. This gives approximately 9.2%.

subject: Economics
text: When demand exceeds supply at the prevailing price, the market experiences
explanation: A shortage occurs when consumers wish to buy more than producers offer at the current price. Competitive pressure tends to push price upward toward equilibrium.

subject: Economics
text: Division of labour tends to raise output because workers
options: Become more specialized in particular tasks
explanation: Division of labour allows workers to concentrate on tasks, develop skill and reduce time lost switching jobs. These effects can improve productivity and total output.
